row.text: The fragmented lexicon continues to cascade, a digital avalanche of semantic debris that defies linear narrative structure. It is as if the collective unconscious of the internet has been distilled into a chaotic stream of consciousness, where the boundaries between code, commerce, and culture dissolve into a singular, pulsating noise. The word "Broadway" hangs suspended in the air, a neon sign flickering in the rain, while "fall" suggests a descent not just of leaves, but of order itself. Into this void, "eing" whispers, a fragment of a German verb, perhaps "eingeben," to input, to enter, to become part of the machine. Disturbance is the primary state; "distur" cuts through the static, a jagged edge of anxiety. The "outbreak" is not biological but informational, a viral spread of meaninglessness that infects every node in the network. Unable to contain the flow, the system "fib" s, constructing false narratives to make sense of the chaos, "Recording" every glitch, every stutter, every moment of hesitation. The "Professor" stands at the podium, lecturing on "Rel" ationships, on the "Halloween" of the digital soul, where masks are worn not to hide
